speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when the injury occurred, and do you feel any numbness or tingling in your foot? REQUEST TEST: X-ray of the right hip and pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_X-ray: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern; let's focus on the mechanism of injury. Did your foot get stuck in a twisted position, and have you noticed any visible deformity or shortening of your right leg compared to the left? REQUEST TEST: MRI of the right hip.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the right hip: No acute fracture lines or marrow edema patterns consistent with a fracture. However, the imaging confirms significant soft tissue swelling and confirms the clinical finding of posterior dislocation of the right hip joint with congruent joint surfaces upon reduction (implied by the absence of fracture and the initial X-ray findings of dislocation).
